I wrote the owner taste profile at `C:\Users\atish\Desktop\mockmob copy\mockmob-next\docs\brain\OWNER-TASTE-PROFILE.md`. It is not committed. It runs about 1,540 words, so with its tables it is a little over the two pages asked for.

It has the four parts you asked for:
1. **What he loves**, with his quotes: HIGH, Revolut, Fampay and Apple Liquid Glass, Opal, Mobi alive and adaptive, bold persuasive copy, one leading action, a unique feel, and a subtle Night.
2. **What he rejects**, as a table with one quote per item. "Decoded strips" did not appear in any of his files. I took it to mean his complaints about things a student has to puzzle out: the road strip (N1), the slider and the grey replay boxes (D17). Correct that row if he meant something else.
3. **The 15-point checklist** below.
4. **How he gives feedback**, plus a fixed one-line note format for critics and a worked example on the swipe stack (D90).

The checklist (a critic applies all 15 to every screen, at 390 and 1440, Night and Day, in use):
1. **Unique:** with the logo covered, it is still MockMob, not a template. Name its one ownable detail.
2. **Premium reference:** it holds up side by side with HIGH, Revolut, Fampay or Apple. Glass is on the chrome and physical; the art is rich, not flat vector stand-ins.
3. **One leading action:** within one glance the student knows the single next tap, and it leads on to the next step.
4. **Self-explaining first run:** a first-time user understands every control without being told. Gestures are shown and coached the first time, sliders look draggable, and buttons look pressable.
5. **No form:** no stacked fields or segmented rows. Settings and plans are guided, interactive steps with a live readout.
6. **Rich, not cut:** against the last approved version, nothing good is lost (mascot moments, full analysis, rich cards). Items on the Keep list are untouched.
7. **Calm structure:** clutter is solved by grouping and layering, not by deleting. Nothing has to be decoded; every dot, bar or indicator carries real information (M-005).
8. **Mobi alive and adaptive:** Mobi reacts to what the student just did, is sized to the free space, and is never cramped, asleep or puzzling.
9. **Copy:** bold, specific, persuasive marketing English. Zero disclaimers, filler or build jargon. Every number is real.
10. **Consistency:** one label per action across the screen, and every count agrees.
11. **Layout safety:** a real gap under the status bar, balanced top and bottom, nothing under the bottom bar. A clear Back button, not only a small icon. Targets of 44 px or more.
12. **Motion:** every state change moves with a purpose; it is springy, interruptible and at least as good as the version before. One indicator slides, never two boxes. A haptic on meaningful moments (app).
13. **Night subtle, Day equal:** no neon, glow, gradient text, pulsing pills or kickers. Night is as quiet as it was before R2.
14. **Instant:** no needless confirm sheets. A tap answers at once, and nothing stays stuck loading.
15. **Visible:** his ask is obviously changed, and the note says exactly where to look. The screen is neither over-gamified nor sparse.

Critic note format:
`[Surface > screen, viewport, theme] VERDICT: KEEP / REFINE / REGRESSION. Like: <what to keep>. See: <what is physically wrong>. Fails: <checklist #> ("his quote"). Fix: <one concrete change with values>. Like in: <reference app>. Where to look: <route or step>.`

results.surface: App > Today (header and Mobi, lead card, length pill, This week, Road to CUET, The weeks ahead, Your marks and Last paper, Weak chapters, Repairs and Revise, Your colleges). Worktree wt-v15-1 (ui/v15.1-1018, 1.0.15+6). Read only. Overall verdict: REFINE. Keep: the lamp-lit 3D object on the lead card, the big number, the volt key, the weeks-ahead timeline with chevrons, the Last paper right/wrong/blank bar, and the error state with a big Mobi. On a real account (device walk, 384 Night) the page reads more like a log than in the goldens. The length shows as three different figures; the header Mobi is a still picture; the week readout prints every paper; the road counts every mock taken as "due". Two blocks have nothing that says they can be tapped.

items.title: Lead card shows three different lengths for one Revise round
items.where: lib/features/today/logic/move_builder.dart _revise() (minutes = size<=5?5:10; selectedMinutes: size; options 5/10); widgets/move_hero.dart _ValueLine/_LengthToken; logic/glance_builder.dart QueueTiles.reviseMinutes
items.why: Checklist #10, one label and agreeing counts (D15: mixed labels are 'a very confusing UI'). On the device the pill says 'about 9 min', the key says 'Start Revise 10 min', the Revise tile says 'Free, about 10 min' and This week says 'about 9 minutes'. The token shows selectedMinutes, which holds the question count (9), but the key rounds up to 10. 9 is also not one of the 5/10 choices, so the length sheet can open with no choice marked as current.
items.change: Pick one figure, 1 min per question. In _revise set minutes = size; primary = TodayCopy.startRevise(size). When 5 < remaining < 10, set options = [DurationChoice(5,5), DurationChoice(remaining, remaining)] so the current length is always a choice. Show the token as exact ('9 min', no 'about') when it equals the key. Give QueueTiles reviseMinutes the same size. Add a unit test that the pill, key, tile and upNext line all give the same number.

results.surface:
App onboarding (welcome, the 7 steps, warm-up question, plan and seal, save step), sign-in (email, code) and the sheet after sign-in. Worktree wt-v15-1, ui/v15.1-1018, 1.0.15+6. Read-only review of the walk round2 (w-02 to w-30), round1 (21a, 21d) and the onboarding and auth golden masters.

Overall verdict: REFINE. Keep: the lamp-lit welcome scene, the foil seal moment, the sheet with its bubbles, the stage road with the live weeks count, the course tiles with real college counts, the warm-up question with its measured seconds, the D47 slider synced with the day bubbles, and Mobi's lines on the marks step ("A trap, not a gap.").

What a first-time student actually hits:
- Taps a subject set, never rates a subject, and the sheet says "all Okay".
- Lands on save, where Google and email are greyed and "Not now" is the only live key.
- Taps "Use an email code" and gets a generic "Sign in" screen that offers Google and Password all over again.
- Reaches Today with nothing telling them what the cards or a left or right swipe mean (D90).

Most fixes are size S.

Summary:
1. Walk 1 showed nine problems in the current build. The main ones: nothing ever shows a first-timer the gesture, only a grey caption. "Do this instead" means nothing when the lead card is off screen. A dead band about 120 dp tall opens under the deck after a skip. There is no undo, and the deck learns nothing from skips. Two copy bugs: the end card always says "tonight", and a repair line reads "All two are" (`copy.dart:98`).
2. The two directions are renamed everywhere (stamp, button, coach line, screen reader): right is **Up next** and left is **Not now**. Right puts the card into the lead card and never starts a session or spends a credit; left sends it to the back, nothing is deleted.
3. Taken from Tinder: the buttons leave the card and sit in one fixed row under the deck, Not now / Undo / Up next. Dragging toward a side makes that button grow and light up, and a stamp with the same words lands on the card.
4. First run: a one-line intro says what the cards are. The top card then demonstrates by itself, right then left, about 2.2 s, once per phone; any touch stops it. Coach lines explain each side, and "Let go" lines show at the threshold. The first right swipe ends with a glass bar, "Nothing starts until you tap Start", with Undo; the first left swipe shows the card tucking in behind the deck.
5. I rejected a separate intro card: it delays the first real card, and swiping it right would have to show "Up next" while nothing moves up.
6. Learning, kept truthful: a small new store on the phone sinks a card kind that was passed on on 2 or more of the last 7 days and not picked since. The suggested card never moves and nothing is removed. The only claim the app makes is "Cards you often pass on sit lower next time", and that line ships only if this store is built.
7. Motion is specified with the app's own motion and spring values: threshold 30% or a 700 dp/s fling, lean x/20, stamp and card-text dimming tied to the drag, the skipped card tucking to the back, the page following the picked card up, and undo as the reverse. There is deliberately no glow ring on the lead card, because Night stays subtle.
8. Haptics use the app's existing set: a tick at the threshold, a light tap when a card is made Up next, nothing during the demo. With reduced motion there is no demo, both meanings show as text, and changes are instant 120 ms fades.
9. Accessibility: 48 dp buttons, Up next and Not now actions on the card itself for TalkBack, spoken announcements after each swipe, a live-region bar whose timer pauses on focus, and at 1.3x text on a 360 dp phone Undo becomes icon-only. Every state is designed, and every string is listed in the spec.
10. The taste check is written in his note format: six findings from my own captures, all fixed in the mock before writing. Still to judge on the device: whether the 72 dp demo reads at 412 dp, whether 5 s is long enough to find Undo, and how a real thumb feels between scrolling and dragging. Build estimate is about 2 h for one Opus agent plus a Sonnet agent in parallel. The one question for the owner is to build it as drawn; my recommendation is yes.
